explanation: The 2010-08-10 FOMC document contains a highly substantive policy shift: the Committee announced it would reinvest principal payments from agency debt and MBS into longer-term Treasury securities to keep the balance sheet constant, reversing the implicit passive tightening that had been underway. This 'QE-lite' decision—preventing balance sheet shrinkage and redirecting flows into Treasuries—was a material easing signal that plausibly caused the structural break detected on 2010-08-17, as markets repriced the path of Fed policy and longer-term interest rates.
